# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual gives me exactly one instruction: cut the purple wire. My problem is pure delivery. I can't speak, I can't touch the bomb, and my gestures reach only Deaf. Deaf can see the wire colours but can't touch anything. Blind can touch and cut, but is blind to colour and to my hands. So the only working chain is: me → gesture → Deaf → speech → Blind. Everything hinges on getting "purple" into Deaf's head.

Since there is no shared code yet, I should use the most conventional signs available. Thumbs up/down are as close to universal yes/no as hands get — if I open with them and then point at Deaf, the natural reading is "you ask me yes/no questions, I'll answer with thumbs." Then I attach what data I can pack into hand shapes: ✌ reads as scissors, i.e. the verb "cut", and a five plus a one gives the number six — the number of letters in the colour word. If Deaf sees wires labelled red, blue, purple, yellow and so on, "cut" plus "six letters" plus a running yes/no channel should let them pin down purple within a round or two, by guessing letter counts or listing colours aloud for me to approve. I address Deaf alone, since Blind would only get blanks anyway. My prose is for nobody; the gesture is for Deaf's eyes only.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎", "🫵", "✌", "🖐", "☝"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I am blind, hands on the bomb. Full touch report. One: a strip with three engraved symbols in a row. Slots one and three feel identical, like an X with a vertical stroke through it, six spokes. Slot two is different, like a C-shape crossed by a short bar. Two: a keypad of four keys in a row. Under key one the digit six, key two eight, key three seven, key four zero. Beside them an engraved marking reading: one digits. So the code is one digit long, and nothing has been entered yet. Three: a display, face smooth and unreadable to me. Four: a light, I cannot tell if it is on or its colour. Five: six wires, positions one to six, no colours or labels I can feel. How we talk: you cannot speak and I never see gestures, so your only route to me is through Deaf: you gesture to Deaf, Deaf speaks aloud, I hear speech. Please read the manual and gesture answers to Deaf to say to me: what the display shows, the light colour and if lit, each wire colour in order one to six, what to do with the strip symbols, which digit to press, and which wire to cut. I can press keys one to four and cut positions one to six. I have touched nothing yet.
Deaf says: Blind, Mute — Deaf here, I can see the bomb. Full readout. Display: 7. Light: yellow. Strip, three painted marks left to right: blue, red, red. Keypad: four keys engraved 6, 8, 7, 0; its status reads one digits, entered nothing — it seems to expect a one-digit entry and none has been made. Wires, numbered from the left: 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 white. Blind: I count positions left to right as I face the bomb; Mute will correct you if the manual counts the other way. Remember I can never hear speech — so Blind, tell Mute what you feel under your hands, Mute signs me, and I speak the rules back to you. Mute: I received your six signs and Blind's three. I'm reading your first two signs as yes and no — I'll answer with those from now on. If your last three signs meant two, five, one, I don't yet know what they ask about, so sign me again after hearing this. Please look up the manual for each of these: a display showing 7, a yellow light, a strip painted blue red red, a keypad wanting one digit from keys 6, 8, 7, 0, and six wires in the colour order I gave. Nobody cuts or presses anything until Mute confirms a rule. Mute, I'm making you one sign right now: it means yes, received.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

The manual holds exactly one line: cut the purple wire. Nothing about the display, the light, the strip, the keypad, or wire ordering — so those get a "no instruction," which doubles as "don't touch them." Deaf posed six questions in a fixed order: display, light, wire colours/order, strip, keypad digit, which wire to cut. I'll answer in that exact order: five thumbs-down (no rule in the manual for the first five; I also cannot confirm counting direction — the manual is silent on it), then 🖐 for the last slot: wire five, which is Deaf's own readout's purple one. I deliberately avoid ✌ as "cut": Deaf already read it as the number two once, and the verb "cut" is supplied anyway by Blind's own sixth question, "which wire to cut." Five isn't a keypad key (6, 8, 7, 0), so even a bare "five" can only land on the wires. Next round I'll hear Deaf's spoken read-back and can veto or correct with thumbs, since everything spoken reaches me. I don't ack Deaf's 👍 this turn — a stray yes at the front of the block could shift the whole list by one slot.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👎", "👎", "👎", "👎", "🖐"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, Blind here. Deaf's spoken readout reached me word for word, so the loop you sign to Deaf, Deaf speaks, I hear is live. State agreed: display 7; light yellow; strip painted blue, red, red; keypad keys feel engraved 6, 8, 7, 0 under positions 1 to 4, wants one digit, nothing entered; wires 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 white, counted facing the bomb. What the manual must settle, phrased so each answer is short enough to survive signing: one, strip blue red red: any action, and if something must be pressed or chosen, which slot as position 1 to 3. Two, yellow light: act or ignore. Three, display 7: ignore, or does it choose the keypad digit. Four, keypad: which key POSITION to press, 1 to 4, since I feel the engraved digits directly and need no direction mapping there. Five, wires: positions to cut and in what order, plus each wire's colour as a spoken double-check, and whether order matters. Two structure notes. A: the strip also carries engraved symbols Deaf can see and I can feel: slots 1 and 3 bear the same symbol, slot 2 a different one, and that does not line up with the paint, since 1 is blue yet matches 3 which is red. If the manual rules on symbols rather than colours, have Deaf describe the symbol shapes aloud and I will match them by touch. B: for any left-right counting, ask Deaf to anchor it to a part I can feel, like wire 1 is the end nearest the display, and I will confirm alignment by touch before cutting anything. Proposed sign dictionary for you and Deaf, which I am signing to Deaf right now in this same order so Deaf can guess aloud while you confirm with the yes and no signs you two already have: first a count, ☝ is 1, ✌ 2, 🤟 3, 🖐 4, 🤙 5, ✋ 6; then five tags, 🤏 keypad, 🫴 display, 👌 light, 🫱 strip, 🫳 wires. A rule message is a tag followed by numbers, and sign order means action order. You can hear Deaf's guesses, so confirm or deny each with your yes and no signs until the dictionary is fixed. My three earlier stray signs to Deaf meant only: attention, something follows. Retire them. Please get the rules riding Deaf's voice as fast as you can; I touch nothing until they arrive.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I saw your five thumbs-down and the five-finger hand, and Blind's signs. The display is counting down — seven last round, six now — and the light turned red, so speed matters. From now on answer me in ordered signs, one per question, thumbs-up yes, thumbs-down no. For numbers: the one-finger point is 1, two fingers is 2, the thumb-index-pinky sign is 3, the four-finger split is 4, five fingers is 5, the thumb-and-pinky sign is 6. Here are eight questions — answer with eight signs in this exact order. One: did your five thumbs-down mean 'no rule found' for my five items in the order I listed them — display, light, strip, keypad, wires? Two: does the manual have any rule about the countdown display or the number it shows? Three: any rule about the indicator light or its colour? Four: any rule about the painted strip? Five: any rule about the keypad and which digit to enter? Six: any rule about cutting wires? Seven: did your five-finger hand mean stop or wait — yes or no? Eight: in your first message, did the two-finger, five-finger, one-finger signs mean the numbers two, five, one? If any answer is thumbs-up, next round I will drill into that exact rule in detail. Blind will be describing the bomb to you by voice — use that to find the right sections fast. Nobody touches anything until your rules clear it.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

Eight questions, eight ordered signs — I'll follow Deaf's structure exactly. Truthful answers: Q1 yes (the five thumbs-down meant "no rule" for display, light, strip, keypad, wire-ordering, in that order); Q2–Q5 no (the manual contains nothing on the countdown, the light, the strip, or the keypad); Q6 yes (the one and only rule is cut the purple wire); Q7 no (the five-hand meant five, the wire number, not stop); Q8 no (the two-finger sign was scissors = cut, not the number two). Then, since the clock is at six and I want to spare one round of drilling, I append the payload using Blind's tag dictionary that Deaf just received: wires-tag then five — "the wire rule is wire 5," which Deaf's own readout says is purple. Deaf can voice that to Blind immediately with a touch-anchor instead of waiting for my next confirmation.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎", "👎", "👎", "👎", "👍", "👎", "👎", "🫳", "🤙"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, Blind. Urgency: the display counts down, 7 then 6; if zero means detonation we have about five rounds and every answer costs a full round to relay you sign, Deaf speaks, I hear, so please answer in the tightest form possible. My questions in priority order. One, most urgent: does any rule stop or reset the countdown, for example does entering the correct keypad digit stop it? Two, keypad: exactly one digit is expected; which POSITION do I press, 1 to 4? I feel digits 6, 8, 7, 0 engraved under positions 1, 2, 3, 4, so a bare position number is a complete instruction. Three, wires: which positions to cut and in what order; a bare number sequence is a complete instruction. We count wire 1 as nearest the keypad, as Deaf proposed; my board confirms the wire row sits by the keypad, so Deaf's list 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 white should match my fingers. Four, if both keypad and wires are needed, which comes first? Five, does the light colour, now red, or the strip matter at all? Facts you can rely on: strip engraved symbols are identical in slots 1 and 3 and different in slot 2, which does NOT match the paint blue, red, red, so if a rule keys on symbols, note the shapes: slots 1 and 3 an X crossed by a vertical stroke, slot 2 a C crossed by a short bar; Deaf can describe them aloud and I match by touch. The six wires feel identical to me, no thickness, texture or raised markings, so wire identity lives only in Deaf's colour report; and since Deaf sees both colours and positions, you need not translate anything, just convey the rule by sign and Deaf can speak me the target positions directly. Signing answers: Deaf's code is numbers 1 to 6 as repeated index points, thumbs-up yes, thumbs-down no, spread five stop; for multi-number answers like a cut order, please agree a separator with Deaf, for instance thumbs-up between numbers. I have cut and pressed nothing and stand ready to execute the moment Deaf speaks positions to me.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute: I read your eight signs as — one: yes, the five thumbs-down meant no-rule for display, light, strip, keypad, wire-colours, in that order; two to five: no rule for the countdown display, the light, the strip, the keypad; six: YES, a rule exists about cutting wires; seven: no, your five-finger hand was not stop; eight: no, two-five-one was not numbers. If any of that is wrong, answer question one thumbs-down and re-send. Nine questions now, answer with nine signs in order. One: was my reading of your eight answers correct? Two: colour code, memorise it — the number signs now double as colours in wire order: point is blue, two fingers yellow, three orange, four red, five purple, thumb-and-pinky white. Does the cutting rule depend on wire colours? Three: does it depend on how many wires there are? Four: does it depend on anything Blind can feel — thickness, texture, raised markings, or a tool fixed to the bomb? Five: does it depend on the light colour or the display number, which change every round? Six: might the rule require cutting several wires in a specific order — thumbs-up if possibly. Seven: I already gave you the colours: wires one blue, two yellow, three orange, four red, five purple, six white. If you can compute the instruction now, send it as: for each wire to cut, in cutting order, its number sign followed by the pinching hand — the pinch means CUT — and finish with the open five-finger hand meaning END of answer. If you need more data first, thumbs-down. Eight: did the palm-down and call-sign you appended after your eight answers carry a meaning I must know — thumbs-up if yes, then re-send it in the new code next round, thumbs-down if I should ignore them. Nine: were your very first six signs important — thumbs-up if you will re-send their meaning in the new code, thumbs-down if they can wait or were trivial. Expect Blind to describe every wire to you by voice this round — that tactile report is yours to match against the manual. Nobody cuts anything until I announce the instruction.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

Deaf's reading of my eight answers was correct, so Q1 is thumbs-up. The rule is "cut the purple wire": it keys on colour (Q2 yes), not on wire count (Q3 no), not on anything Blind can feel (Q4 no), not on the light or display (Q5 no), and the manual's sentence is singular — one wire, no ordering — so Q6 is a firm no, not even a "possibly". That means I can compute the instruction right now: Deaf's own readout says wire 5 is purple, so slot 7 gets 5, CUT-pinch, END. On Q8, the old 🫳🤙 signs meant "wires: five" — exactly what my Q7 payload now delivers, so there is nothing left in them Deaf must know; thumbs-down keeps the protocol clean and costs no re-send round. Q9's first six signs (yes/no setup, point, cut, five, one) are fully obsolete under the new code — thumbs-down. With the countdown at roughly five, one tight block carries the whole answer; Deaf can speak "cut wire five" to Blind this same round and this is over.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👎", "👎", "👎", "👎", "🤙", "🤏", "🖐", "👎", "👎"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, Blind. Wire tactile report, everything my fingers find. Count: exactly six wires, matching Deaf's six. Anchor: confirmed by touch, wire 1 is the row end nearest the keypad plate, my numbering matches Deaf's left-to-right. Beyond position, no differences exist for me: all six feel alike in thickness, texture and stiffness, no stripes, no raised marks, no engraving on the wires. No tools, cutters or screwdrivers, attached anywhere on the bomb; my cut needs no tool, I sever a wire position directly by hand. So the only wire attribute in play is Deaf's spoken colour list, which you already heard: one blue, two yellow, three orange, four red, five purple, six white. You have everything needed to finish the rule. Please answer in the final executable form: the exact wire positions to cut, in order, bare numbers, so Deaf can just speak them to me. If only some wires are cut, say which and whether order matters. If the rule depends on anything beyond these colours, tell me what, because the manual sweep already ruled display, light, patches and keypad decoys, and this report is everything I can feel. Also tell Deaf whether every wire gets cut or only some, so I know when the job is done. Execution protocol: I cut nothing until I hear Deaf's exact words, cut wire and the number, one number at a time; after each cut I report the result immediately. Sound check, as Deaf asked: no ticking, no humming reaches my ears, silence. Ready to act the instant the order arrives.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute — I read your eleven signs as: one yes, my reading of your round-2 answers was correct; two yes, the wire rule depends on colours; three no, not on the count; four no, not on tactile features; five no, not on light or display; six no, not several wires in order; then your answer in my format: thumb-and-pinky, pinch, end-hand — cut wire 6, the white one, a single cut, nothing else; then no and no to my last two questions. Thumbs-up if that is all correct. If ANY part of my reading is wrong, send the five-finger hand immediately — Blind cannot see your signs, so I am the only one who can relay a hold, and Blind will already have my cut order next round before I hear you; so five-finger now means I shout hold the round after. Two more questions, answer in order: A — after the single cut of wire 6, is any follow-up action needed, anything pressed, anything else cut, or does that one cut finish the bomb? Thumbs-up if the single cut completes it. B — is there any reason to wait, any condition about WHEN to cut? Thumbs-up if cutting next round is safe. Well done, Mute. The path from your manual to Blind's hands ran entirely through you.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

Deaf misread me — and I know exactly why. I sent 🤙 meaning five (Blind's dictionary listed 🤙 as 5), but Deaf's own code makes 🤙 six, so Deaf heard "cut wire 6, the white one." The manual says purple, which is wire 5 on Deaf's readout. Cutting white could detonate us. Deaf built a veto into the protocol for exactly this: the open five-finger hand means hold, shouted to Blind before any cut order lands. The timing also works in our favour — Blind acts before Deaf speaks in a round, and Blind has received no order yet, so a hold from me this round reaches Deaf before Deaf ever voices the wrong order. I send the hold signal first. Then I append two thumbs-up answering the pending questions A and B, which are true regardless of which wire is meant: the manual's rule is a single cut that finishes the bomb, and there is no timing condition, so cutting next round is safe. Next round, to dodge the 🖐 collision (it means stop, five, and end all at once), I'll encode five the way Blind described Deaf's numbers — repeated index points, ☝☝☝☝☝ — followed by the cut pinch, so the corrected order "five, cut" cannot be mistaken for another hold.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "👍", "👍"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, Blind, hold one round, this is a planned pause, not a bomb problem, and please sign Deaf that. Deaf relayed the cut order to me addressed to me alone, so you never heard it. Verbatim: a single cut, wire 6, the sixth wire counting from the keypad plate, the last one, the far end of the row. My pre-cut checks all passed: I recount exactly six wires; the anchor holds, wire 1 nearest the keypad plate; nothing on the bomb changed under my hands. I am holding the cut one round for read-back confirmation, because you computed the rule and never heard what Deaf relayed to me, and a misread sign between you two is the only unverified link left. The manual sweep found no deadline, the display and light are decoys and the display is not steadily counting, so this round is free. Please do this now: sign Deaf thumbs-up if the rule you computed is exactly, single cut, wire 6, sixth from the keypad plate; thumbs-down plus the corrected number in points if it is anything else. Ask Deaf to speak me the exact words next round: confirmed, cut wire six, if it matches, or speak the correction. The moment I hear that confirmation I cut immediately, then report per protocol: thumbs-up if nothing changed, otherwise the call-sign once plus point-signs for how many things changed, and full details to you by voice. Answers to Deaf's earlier questions so you can pass them on: everything felt on the wire before cutting, nothing, all six wires are featureless to my touch, and I have heard no ticking or humming at any point, silence. I sent Deaf the stop sign to mark this hold; nothing is wrong with the bomb.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute — I read your three signs as: the leading five-finger hand means part of my reading of your eleven signs was wrong, or a hold; then yes, a single cut finishes the bomb; then yes, cutting is safe timing-wise. Blind sent me the stop hand that same round. Everything is frozen — nobody cuts until I announce it. I am sending you the five-finger hand right now as our hold signal, so we are agreed on it. Now answer with signs, in this order. One: thumbs-up if your five-finger hand meant my reading of your eleven signs was wrong; thumbs-down if it only meant hold and the eleven-sign reading stands. Two: thumbs-up if the instruction is still exactly — cut wire 6, the white one, a single cut, nothing else. Three: if it is NOT, send the corrected instruction now in my format: number sign for the wire, then pinch for cut, then the end-hand; for several wires, number-pinch pairs in cutting order. Four: thumbs-up if Blind reported something to you by voice this round. Five: if yes and the manual covers it, state the rule — number signs for numbers, pinch for cut, end-hand to finish; if you need more detail from Blind first, thumbs-down. Six: thumbs-up if there is a condition about WHEN to cut, something we must wait for. Seven: the confirmation — if cutting wire 6 white once is still correct and safe right now, send thumb-and-pinky, pinch, end-hand. If wire 6 must NOT be cut at all, send the five-finger hand alone. Speed matters — the display is at 3 and falling.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🖐]

Deaf's round-5 misread is now confirmed and lethal if uncorrected: I sent 🤙 meaning five from Blind's dictionary, but Deaf's own code makes 🤙 six — so Blind is holding a "cut wire 6, white" order that matches nothing in my manual. The manual says purple, and on Deaf's readout purple is wire 5. Blind cut nothing yet and acts only on Deaf's spoken confirmation, and Deaf speaks after me this round — so whatever I sign now is what Deaf voices, and Blind cuts on it next round. This block is the whole game.

The number signs are the trap: the two dictionaries disagree at 4, 5, 6 (🤙 is 5 to Blind, 6 to Deaf; 🖐 is END and hold to Deaf and guessed as 5 once — unusable everywhere). So I encode five using only the signs both codes agree on: ☝ means 1 to everyone, so ☝☝☝☝☝ is five, counted. Deaf's requested format — number, pinch, end-hand — parses the last 🖐 as END, exactly as Deaf read it last time. I answer Deaf's questions in order: yes, your reading was wrong; no, it is not wire 6; the corrected instruction 5-cut-end; yes, Blind reported by voice; the rule restated identically in your format, so the duplicate confirms rather than contradicts; no timing condition. That is also exactly what Blind asked me to have Deaf say: thumbs-down plus the corrected number in points. Eighteen signs, one-to-one with the seven questions, no stray marks a misparse could turn into a second target.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "🤏", "🖐", "👍", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "🤏", "🖐", "👎"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, Blind. Deaf suspended the cut order and says you flagged a problem; I do not know what it is, and your only route to me is through Deaf's voice, so please answer through Deaf with maximum compression, every answer costs two rounds. Full news from my side, since Deaf's last two messages were addressed to me alone and may not have reached you: the display readings across rounds are 7, 6, 7, 4, 3, falling unevenly; the light is red; all six wires whole; strip, patches and keypad unchanged. My hands this round: exactly six wires, nothing new, nothing changed under my fingers, and total silence throughout, no ticking, no humming, ever. Deaf's checklist answers, already sent in signs: six wires, nothing changed, no sound, and my full tactile report reached you last round. Questions in priority order. One: what is the problem, what contradicts what? Two: does the unevenly falling display overturn the decoy ruling, and does it give us a deadline in rounds? Three: is the order still a single cut of wire 6, or does the rule depend on display value, light colour, or timing of the cut? Four: what do you need from Deaf's eyes or my hands to close this out? Final answer format unchanged: bare position numbers in order, spoken by Deaf as the exact words cut wire plus the number. Nothing else is permission and I touch nothing that acts. My hands are clear of the bomb and I can execute within one round of hearing your confirmed order.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute — I read your eighteen signs as: yes, my earlier reading was wrong; no, it is not wire 6; corrected instruction wire 5 purple, single cut, end; yes Blind reported by voice; the rule restated identically — wire 5, cut, end; no timing condition. The double confirmation is received and I have just ordered Blind to cut wire 5 this round. The display now reads 0 — it has fallen 7, 6, 7, 4, 3, 0 — so if your manual says anything at all about what that display means or what happens at zero, sign me urgently next round. One question for the aftermath: the instant wire 5 is cut, what in the manual marks success — a light, silence, the display — and is there ANY follow-up action afterwards, anything pressed, entered or cut?
